pages.title: Quickstart
pages.summary: Connect an agent, check your account, and make your first image or video.

sections.title: 1. Connect your agent
paragraphs: Add the hosted Agent Media connector to your client, then complete the browser sign-in yourself. Use the connection guide for Claude, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor and other MCP clients.

sections.title: 2. Check your account
paragraphs: Ask the agent to check your connection and available balance with get_account. If that tool is absent from an older connector catalog, list_models includes the same account check. These checks do not spend, refill or grant credits.
sections.code: Check my Agent Media account and show the available models. Do not generate anything yet.
sections.note: Generation requires paid credits. A successful connection or upload does not include free generation.

sections.title: 3. Describe the result
paragraphs: Tell the agent what you want to make, the subject, the setting, the output shape and whether to use a reference. You can start with a simple image before attempting a longer video.
sections.code: I want a vertical product image of my bottle on a clean bathroom counter, in soft morning light. Use my uploaded photo to keep the product consistent. Show me the generation quote first.

sections.title: 4. Add reference images
paragraphs: Ask for the existing upload panel. Drag in one or more images, then tell the agent you are done. The agent retrieves the uploaded image URLs and passes them to the generation tool. Uploading alone is not permission to generate.

sections.title: 5. Review the cost and generate
paragraphs: The agent quotes the intended model and inputs, checks the balance, and submits within your approved budget. It then polls the returned job ID until the output is ready. If a status check fails, it should keep checking the same job instead of starting another.
sections.note: Keep the job ID until you have the final result. A timeout is not proof that generation failed.

pages.title: Core concepts
pages.summary: Understand the account, connector, tools, models and jobs before your first run.

sections.title: Your account
paragraphs: The hosted account owns your credits, generations and temporary upload sessions. Connecting an agent authorizes it to act on that account. Do not paste account keys, login codes or storage credentials into shared chats.

sections.title: Connector and public skill
paragraphs: The MCP connector exposes callable tools. The public skill explains how to use them together. Installing a skill alone does not establish the authenticated connector connection.

sections.title: Tools and models
paragraphs: A tool is an action such as generating an image, quoting a request or checking a job. A model is the provider-backed engine used for that action. Video modes determine whether the input is a text prompt, a starting frame or references.

sections.title: Asynchronous jobs
paragraphs: Generation returns a job ID before the media is finished. Poll that ID with get_run_status. Keep the original ID through delays and status errors; creating a new request can create another paid run.

sections.title: Quotes and credits
paragraphs: A quote estimates the intended request. The account balance is a snapshot, not a reservation. Generation performs the final credit checks. Connection checks, quotes and temporary uploads do not grant credits.

pages.title: Upload reference images
pages.summary: Drag and drop multiple images, then use them in a generation.

sections.title: Open the existing upload panel
paragraphs: Ask your agent to open Agent Media’s upload panel. It should call open_upload_panel when available, or upload_image with an empty object for an older cached catalog. Use the returned browser link if the client cannot display the embedded panel.
sections.code: Open the Agent Media image upload panel. I want to upload reference photos. Do not generate yet.

sections.title: Drop in your images
paragraphs: Drop one or more images into the panel, or choose them using the file picker. A session accepts up to 10 images, up to 25 MB each. Wait until each upload is marked ready and check the displayed expiry. The panel supports images, not video or audio.
sections.note: Use still PNG, JPEG or WebP images. Convert unsupported formats such as HEIC or SVG to a supported still image.

sections.title: Use the images in generation
paragraphs: Tell the agent when the images are ready. It retrieves them with get_uploads, or the panel retrieval instructions returned by upload_image. It must pass the exact returned image URLs into the next generation.
steps: Image editing or composition: use refs in generate_image.
Start a video from one photo: use first_frame in generate_video.
Reference-guided video: use refs with a model and mode that supports them.
Quote the intended inputs and continue only within the generation you authorized.

sections.title: Private storage and 24-hour expiry
paragraphs: Images are stored temporarily in private object storage and accessed through restricted URLs. The session and all its image URLs expire 24 hours after the session was created; an image added later has less time remaining. Anyone holding a valid restricted image URL can use it until it expires, so treat it as private. Re-upload an expired reference before another generation.
sections.note: A local file path, an attachment visible in chat, or an expired URL is not a usable generation reference.

sections.title: If the agent stops after upload
paragraphs: Tell it to retrieve the uploaded images and use their returned URLs in the generation you already requested. It should not build another upload page or ask you to paste base64 into chat.
sections.code: Use the images from this Agent Media upload session as references for the generation I requested. Retrieve their URLs, quote the request, and continue within my approved budget.

pages.title: Account and billing
pages.summary: Paid generation, balance checks and recovering your place after checkout.

sections.title: Generation uses paid credits
paragraphs: Hosted generation requires credits. Account checks, model discovery, quotes and temporary image uploads use no generation credits; they do not give you free credits. Use the current pricing page and the actual request quote to understand cost.

sections.title: Check the actual balance
paragraphs: Ask your agent to call get_account. A positive balance still needs to be compared with the quoted cost. If the check is unavailable, retry it; do not assume the balance is zero or purchase again because of a temporary error.

sections.title: After a payment
paragraphs: Payment fulfillment updates the account on the server. A checkout return URL or a “success” query parameter is not proof that the balance has been credited. If the balance has not updated, check billing and your payment before making another purchase.

sections.title: Continue where you left off
paragraphs: The dashboard retains the destination that onboarding or checkout interrupted. Billing offers Continue creating. Skill forms can restore drafts for up to 24 hours in the same browser tab and account. Review the restored inputs before running; returning never starts a paid generation automatically.
sections.note: Closing the tab or disabling browser storage can prevent draft recovery. Temporary image URLs keep their own expiry.

sections.title: Account recovery without a plan
paragraphs: Signed-in users can reach billing and settings before completing onboarding or buying a plan. Use settings to manage your account and connection configuration.

pages.title: How agents should work
pages.summary: A reliable sequence from a user request to finished media.

sections.title: Discover before choosing
paragraphs: Read the actual tool catalog. Check account readiness with get_account, then use list_models to choose the kind, model and supported mode. Use the current public skill for detailed prompting and tool guidance.

sections.title: Resolve inputs
paragraphs: For user images, use the existing upload panel and retrieve the returned URLs. Reference images belong in refs or first_frame according to the intended model/mode; describing an image in the prompt does not attach it.

sections.title: Quote the intended request
paragraphs: Call quote with the same model and relevant inputs you intend to submit. Compare the quote with the account balance and stay within the user-approved budget. An upload-only request is not authorization to spend.

sections.title: Submit once, then track
paragraphs: Submit the generation and preserve the returned job ID. Poll that same ID until completion. Keep any request identity when recovering a lost response; changing it can create a new paid run.

sections.title: Return the result
paragraphs: Give the user the finished media using the client’s supported output display. If the run fails, report the saved job ID and the actual error. Do not claim a refund or successful output unless the service confirms it.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.summary: Start with the symptom, recover the existing work, and avoid duplicate payments.

sections.title: The agent cannot see the tools
paragraphs: Confirm the Agent Media connector is enabled for that conversation and complete sign-in. Refresh or reconnect the connector if the client keeps an old catalog, then start a fresh conversation. Installing only the public skill is not enough.

sections.title: The upload panel is missing
paragraphs: Ask the agent to call upload_image with an empty object if open_upload_panel is absent. Use the returned browser link when the client cannot embed the panel. Do not build a replacement uploader.

sections.title: The uploaded image is ignored
paragraphs: Have the agent retrieve the uploaded URLs and pass them as refs or first_frame. Check that the chosen model supports that input mode. Uploading an image does not automatically attach it to every later request.

sections.title: An image reference expired
paragraphs: Temporary images expire with their upload session, 24 hours after the session was created. Open a new panel or follow the current session’s instructions, re-upload the image, and use the new URL.

sections.title: Credits seem missing
paragraphs: Run get_account or the account check included in list_models. A temporarily unavailable lookup is not a zero balance. Check billing before paying again; keep the payment reference private when contacting support.

sections.title: Generation timed out or status failed
paragraphs: Keep the original job ID and retry get_run_status. A status outage does not mean the generation failed. Do not submit a second paid request to check the first.

sections.title: What to include in a support request
paragraphs: Include the client, tool name, approximate time, job or upload-session ID, and the visible error code. Never post API keys, login codes, upload-panel tokens, restricted image URLs or customer-private images in a public issue.

pages.title: Jobs, errors and retries
pages.summary: Recover the original request instead of accidentally generating twice.

sections.title: Keep request identity and job IDs
paragraphs: For MCP generate_image, generate_video and generate_audio, pass request_id. For POST /v2/generate/:kind, send the Idempotency-Key header. Generate a fresh identity for each intended generation and save it with the exact inputs before submitting. Reuse both after a lost response. A retry returns the original job without another debit; changed inputs under the same identity return HTTP 409. This protection does not cover every fixed recipe.

sections.title: An uncertain acknowledgement
paragraphs: If a generation response returns an accepted job but says worker acknowledgement is uncertain, poll that job. Do not infer failure or assume a refund.

sections.title: Temporary status failures
paragraphs: HTTP 503 STATUS_UNAVAILABLE means status could not be read. Respect Retry-After and retry the original job ID. HTTP 404 after an authenticated, successful lookup means the job was not found for that account.

sections.title: Temporary account failures
paragraphs: HTTP 503 ACCOUNT_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE means the balance is unknown. Retry the check; do not treat it as zero. Quotes and balance snapshots do not reserve credits or guarantee provider availability.

sections.title: Report confirmed outcomes
paragraphs: Provider and generation failures should be reported with their actual error and job ID. Only tell a user that credits were refunded when the service confirms it.

pages.title: Self-hosting
pages.summary: Run the open-source platform with your own infrastructure and provider credentials.

sections.title: What is open source
paragraphs: The official repository contains the platform, API, workers, CLI, SDKs and public skill. The separate hosted marketing website is maintained privately. Self-hosting uses your own provider accounts and infrastructure; provider usage may still cost money.

sections.title: Start with the repository
paragraphs: Follow the repository’s current self-hosting instructions and environment example. The supplied Compose stack includes the Supabase services, database, workflow engine, storage and application services. A bare database is not enough.
sections.code:
git clone https://github.com/gitroomhq/agent-media-app.git
cd agent-media-app
cp .env.example .env
# Configure your provider keys and deployment settings in .env
docker compose up

sections.title: Configure the deployment
paragraphs: Keep provider keys and service credentials on the server. Read the environment example for supported replacements, then check database migrations, API health, worker connectivity and storage access before allowing traffic.

sections.title: Enable temporary uploads deliberately
paragraphs: Temporary upload storage must be private and enforce the application expiry. Configure the dedicated bucket and lifecycle cleanup using the OSS deployment guide. Do not expose storage credentials to the upload panel.

sections.title: Hosted credits and self-hosting
paragraphs: Self-host billing configuration is separate from the hosted Agent Media account. Turning off application billing does not make provider generation free or award hosted credits. Review your provider billing before running jobs.

pages.title: Contributing
pages.summary: Improve the maintained public platform and its documentation.

sections.title: Work in the official repository
paragraphs: Use gitroomhq/agent-media-app for platform fixes, public docs and public-skill changes. Read CONTRIBUTING.md and the relevant architecture and service docs before editing.

sections.title: Keep code and generated guidance aligned
paragraphs: The shared schemas and tool definitions drive generated agent guidance and model documentation. Regenerate affected artifacts and run the relevant tests so the published docs agree with tools/list.
sections.code:
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm test
pnpm --filter api-v2 gen:public-skill

sections.title: Make issues reproducible
paragraphs: Describe the expected and actual behavior, affected client, version and a minimal reproduction. Redact credentials, restricted URLs and private customer content. Avoid running paid generations solely to reproduce a report unless the spend is authorized.

sections.title: Edit these guides
paragraphs: The guide content is maintained in docs/public-guides.json in the OSS repository. Detailed tool and model data comes from the generated public-skill/site-data.json. Changes should explain the current behavior and state limitations accurately.
